items.name: Saltwater crocodile
items.blurb: The biggest living reptile. It lives in rivers and coasts from India to northern Australia, and it can swim far out to sea.
clues: Its IUCN conservation status is "Least concern".
It can swim hundreds of kilometres across the open sea.
Its bite is one of the strongest ever measured.
Large males can be over 6 metres long.
It is common in northern Australian rivers.
It is the biggest living reptile.

questions.prompt: What does a tadpole grow into?
questions.explain: Tadpoles are baby frogs and toads that live in water.

questions.prompt: Put a frog's life cycle in order.
questions.explain: Tadpoles grow legs and absorb their tails.

questions.prompt: How can you tell an alligator from a crocodile?
questions.answer: An alligator has a wide, U-shaped snout
questions.explain: Crocodiles have narrower, V-shaped snouts and show more teeth.

questions.prompt: What is the biggest living reptile?
questions.explain: Big males can exceed 6 m and 1,000 kg.
Komodo dragons can be about 3 m long.
Frogs are amphibians; they start life in water.

questions.prompt: Chameleons can move each eye on its own.
questions.explain: They can look in two directions at once.

questions.prompt: Why were cane toads brought to Australia in 1935?
questions.answer: To eat beetles on sugar cane
questions.explain: It failed, and the toads spread across northern Australia.
